impact:
When the primary fails and the secondary serves (degradeCode/degradePlan), the result's session_id belongs to the secondary and is recorded under that provider, but the composite presents as the primary. The next call passing that session_id is rejected — correct guard in MCP, broken workflow: degraded review → unusable session_id. Fix: warn in the degraded result, or route resumes to whichever leaf owns the session instead of always the primary. Same applies to plain failover mode.

LIVE-CONFIRMED 2026-07-01 (probe loop, CLI against dist 1.4.0): with codex primary pointing at a dead binary (codex_path=/nonexistent), deliberate review degraded to Gemini and returned session 045f02a1…; the immediate next `review-code --session <that id>` hard-failed with PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE — resume routed to the dead primary with no failover, even though Gemini (the session owner) was healthy and could have continued it. Bug category: cross-layer trust violation (composite assumes primary owns every session; degrade path violates that).
title: Degraded deliberation returns a session_id the next call cannot continue
